html:
Back to the Dog: Buster

A Russell terrier who chews remotes, bites ankles and jumps on everything. So I named a program after him.

Buster: a Chaos Filter for HEART

It sits in front of a server and tampers with its answers on purpose. Each plugin breaks one rule of the spec and says what ARTIE must do about it.

Every Mutation Judged

Pass or FAIL, from ARTIE’s next requests. Seeded, so any failure replays exactly. Nothing corrupted is ever cached.

He tests ARTIE’s resilience, just as he tests mine.

Basically Unstoppable Saboteur Terrierizing Every Representation
Buster doesARTIE must
Forges the ETagrevalidate, or take the 412 and re-sync
Flips one letter in a formrefuse the bytes, fetch them again
Drops an affordancenever act on it
Strips the forms integritynever follow that link
Lies about the rungtreat it as L0, no forms

Five of the eight plugins in the HEART pack.
say: Recall the dog. His name is Buster. He's a Russell terrier; he chews remotes, bites ankles, and jumps on everything. Fitting, given how much of this was built through /remote-control. So I named a program after him. Buster is a chaos filter that sits in front of a server and tampers with its answers on purpose: the Basically Unstoppable Saboteur Terrierizing Every Representation. Each plugin breaks one rule of the HEART spec, and says what a well-behaved client must do about it. Forge the ETag, and ARTIE has to revalidate or take the 412 and re-sync. Flip one letter in a form, and ARTIE has to refuse the bytes and fetch them again. Drop an affordance, and ARTIE must never act on it. Every mutation ends as a pass or a FAIL, and every one is seeded, so any failure replays exactly. Nothing corrupted is ever cached. Notice that this is the same idea as the hooks: I can't watch ARTIE every minute either, so something else does. Buster tests ARTIE's resilience, just as he tests mine. So what did all of this cost, and how was it built, a few sentences at a time?
